display_name: Penfolds Bin 2 Mataro, South Eastern Australia
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Mataro-led blend from McLaren Vale that pairs Syrah spice with Monastrell chew and Mediterranean savory grip. The wine reads like warm-coast fruit tempered by terra rossa and limestone pockets along the Mount Lofty foothills, which is why it tastes peppery, saline and dense at 14.5% ABV.",
  "wine_summary": "Bin 2 Mataro is Penfolds' Salute to Mediterranean varieties planted and sourced within South Eastern Australia with a focus on McLaren Vale parcels. The label matters because it puts Monastrell (Mataro) forward—an underrepresented variety in mainstream Australian blends—so you get its characteristic gamey, olive and tannic profile married to riper Shiraz flesh. McLaren Vale's combination of terra rossa over limestone, rendzina and patches of dark cracking clay gives this blend a mix of red-fruit ripeness, iron/stone lift and structural grip that defines its palate.",
  "terroir_expression": "McLaren Vale's warm Mediterranean climate, moderated by Gulf St Vincent sea breezes and diurnal cooling from elevations between 50–350m, produces ripe black fruit and fully developed phenolics at high sugar levels; the terra rossa over limestone and rendzina contribute brightness and an iron/mineral thread, while red-brown earth and dark cracking clays supply weight and tannic extraction—together delivering dark, concentrated fruit, peppery rotundone note and a saline-savoury lift.",
  "vinification_summary": "Public winemaking specifics for Bin 2 Mataro are limited; Penfolds historically blends parcels to balance ripeness and structure and then ages in oak to integrate tannin. Expect extended maceration (skin contact to extract color, tannin and spice compounds) and some oak maturation; those choices push the wine toward ripe fruit concentration with rounded mid-palate weight while preserving the peppery, savory signature of Monastrell.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken — the wine's pepper and alcohol cut through the chile oil and stand up to crispy skin; Lamb shoulder with rosemary and char — fattiness and herbaceousness match the Monastrell's gamey tannins and the Shiraz fruit; Olive tapenade on grilled sourdough — mirrors the wine's olive/tapenade notes and amplifies savory tension; Beef short ribs braised in red wine — the wine's tannin and body equal the richness and meld with reduced jus; Charred eggplant with miso and smoked chili (fine dining) — smoky-savoury notes echo the wine's smoked meat and olive profile while acidity keeps it lively.",
  "comparable_wines": "Yangarra Old Vine Mataro — similar Mataro focus and McLaren Vale provenance, with the same peppery, savory spine; d'Arenberg Stump Jump Shiraz — comparable warm-climate McLaren Vale richness and value positioning, though Stump Jump is Shiraz-led rather than Mataro-fronted.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry red with firm tannins and savory, peppery depth",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink within 3–12 years of vintage; store at 12–14°C on its side with 60–70% humidity to avoid cork drying and maintain freshness.",
  "value_assessment": "Price: AUD 25–45. Competitors at this price point include Yangarra Old Vine Mataro (AUD 30–45) and d'Arenberg Stump Jump Shiraz (AUD 15–25). The wine is worth the price if you want bold, McLaren Vale fruit with a clear Monastrell-driven savory backbone; it's not worth it if you seek subtle, low-alcohol Syrah.",
  "market_position": "This sits on casual and regional bistro lists and in retail sections aimed at consumers who prefer bold Australian reds; it also appeals to drinkers looking to explore Monastrell without stepping into small-producer rarity pricing. Expect it in metropolitan wine shops, mainstream restaurant by-the-glass programs, and as a reliable shelf pick for barbecues and hearty meals.",
  "insider_take": "Treat Bin 2 Mataro as a text-book, fruit-forward McLaren Vale crowd-pleaser that leans into Monastrell's olive and tannic personality; many buyers expect Old World peppery restraint, but this is warmer-climate power with clear savory edges. If you want subtlety and cool-climate pepper, buy a Northern Rhône Syrah instead.",
  "aging_potential_years": 8,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 3,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 12,
  "sensory": {
    "acidity": 2,

    "color_intensity": "deep",
    "aroma_intensity": "pronounced",
    "finish_length": "long",
    "complexity": "moderate",

  }
}

parsed.insider_take: Treat Bin 2 Mataro as a text-book, fruit-forward McLaren Vale crowd-pleaser that leans into Monastrell's olive and tannic personality; many buyers expect Old World peppery restraint, but this is warmer-climate power with clear savory edges. If you want subtlety and cool-climate pepper, buy a Northern Rhône Syrah instead.
